chunks: Never set foot in that place. Only a mosque whose foundations have been laid from the very first on godliness is worthy of your visiting it. There you will find men who wish to be purified; and God loves those who are pure.

key_terms.التَّقْوَىٰ: God-consciousness or piety, the spiritual foundation of the mosque
key_terms.الْمُطَهِّرِينَ: Those who are pure, loved by God
key_terms.يَتَطَهَّرُوا: To purify themselves, referring to ritual and spiritual cleanliness

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'mosque founded on piety' in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a divine endorsement of the Mosque of Quba, established by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) upon his arrival in Medina, serving as the archetype for all mosques founded on piety. The mention of 'men who love to purify themselves' is linked to the concept of *taharah* encompassing both physical cleanliness and spiritual rectitude, a theme central to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings. This contrast underscores that the validity of worship depends not merely on the structure but on the spiritual state and intention of the worshippers.
